video.title: The Simplest AI Side Hustle for Beginners

summary: Chris Koerner shows a beginner AI side hustle for garage door repair owners: build an instant quote generator and a job profit tracker with Lovable (no code), plus an after-hours AI voice answering agent in GoHighLevel. He scrapes about 513 Google Maps listings with Outscraper for $111, filters to mobile numbers, cold-texts 50 owners via Straight Text, and gets roughly 40-50% replies and one 'yes' within an hour. He pitches $50 per closed lead with no upfront cost and extrapolates to $100k/month, which is hypothetical. Key takeaway: lead with a low-risk offer, validate with real outreach before building, and use no-code/AI tools to ship fast. Lovable is a channel sponsor and the cold SMS method is illegal in the UK for sole traders.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrates the build and outreach live.

ideas.name: AI after-hours voice answering agent for garage door repair companies
ideas.one_liner: Set up a GoHighLevel AI voice agent that answers missed after-hours calls for garage door repairers, captures name and address, and charges per closed lead or a monthly fee.
ideas.business_model: Per-lead fee (pitched $50 per closed lead) with possible later monthly retainer; Chris also mentions $20-$200 per lead or hundreds per month.
ideas.customer: Owners of small garage door repair businesses (Dallas-Fort Worth in the demo) who miss after-hours calls.
ideas.problem: Owners are on job sites or off duty with phones on silent, so after-hours leads go to voicemail and are lost to competitors; 78% of customers hire the first company to quote.
ideas.offer: A 24/7 AI voice agent that answers calls, collects name and address, emails a call summary and transcript, and can forward urgent callers to the owner. Free setup, no contract, pay only when a lead closes.

pricing.model: Pay per closed lead (test offer), possibly monthly retainer later
pricing.notes: Chris says he may add contracts, upfront money or a retainer later; the first offer is deliberately low-risk.

acquisition_channels.details: Scraped Google Maps with Outscraper, kept mobile numbers only, and bulk-texted 50 owners from Straight Text with a short message ('Hey, I'm here in Dallas. Do you still fix garage doors? I found you on Google Maps'), then sent the pitch to those who replied.

quote.text: Do you answer your phone after hours? The reason I ask is because I created an AI voice agent that will
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Google Maps listings used as the lead source, not as an inbound channel.

ideas.delivery: Agent built in GoHighLevel's Voice AI with a custom prompt/knowledge base generated by ChatGPT. Each client gets a dedicated or ported phone number, a workflow forwards urgent callers to the owner (with secondary and tertiary fallbacks), and emails with transcripts go to agency and owner.
unit_economics_claims: Setup took a couple of minutes; GoHighLevel AI employee has a 30-day free trial
Total validation spend under $100 (scrape plus texting software)
ideas.startup_cost: Under $100 to validate (scrape cost $111 in the demo, GoHighLevel 30-day free trial for the AI employee)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; first 'yes' reply came in under an hour but no money was collected

acquisition.how: Lead scraping and list cleaning can be scripted, but the demonstrated channel is unsolicited SMS, which is unlawful in the UK for sole traders and individuals under PECR. A legal UK version would use cold email to limited companies or inbound ads/SEO, and replies would still need a human or agent to handle.

onboarding.how: Agent creation, number provisioning and prompt generation are largely templated; a human checks the knowledge base and ports numbers.

delivery.how: Once configured, the voice agent answers calls, logs transcripts and forwards urgent calls with no human involvement; occasional prompt tuning is needed.

billing.how: Per-closed-lead billing needs the owner to report which leads closed, which is hard to automate; a flat monthly fee via Stripe would be near-unattended.

support.how: Owners will need help with call handling and disputes over lead attribution; AI can handle first-line questions.

uk_applicability.notes: Voice agents work in the UK, but the cold SMS method breaches PECR for sole traders; UK suppliers would use limited-company cold email or TPS-screened calls. Call-recording and AI disclosure rules (UK GDPR) apply. Market is smaller and Google Maps categories differ.

risks: Owners may not close enough jobs to pay per-lead fees; attribution disputes
Cold SMS legality in the UK
Chris notes most deals never close

tactics.name: Scrape, clean and mobile-filter a local lead list
steps: Use Outscraper's Google Maps scraper with the keyword and a handful of local cities, max 1,000 results, phone not blank
Export to Google Sheets and delete unneeded columns, keeping name, website, address and phone
Standardise phone numbers by removing +1 and dashes
Remove duplicates on phone number (multi-location companies)
Sort by line type and keep only confirmed mobile numbers
Use conditional formatting for 'repair' in the name to prioritise likely repair businesses

quote.text: I'm only going to keep these cell phone numbers.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Short validating first message
steps: Keep the first text under 160 characters
Only validate that they own the business first; don't pitch
Phrase as 'do you still fix...' to prompt a yes
Include your first name and local city
Add varied city names as a custom variable to vary the messages
Wait until all 50 are sent before replying

quote.text: I'm just trying to validate that they own the business that I think they own first. We'll get to the sales pitch later.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Low-risk launch offer
steps: Offer no contracts, no upfront money and free setup
Charge only when a lead closes (e.g. $50)
Raise prices or add retainers later once demand is proven

quote.text: I don't want the price to get in the way of the business being successful or not.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use ChatGPT to write the Lovable prompt and the voice agent prompt
steps: Ask ChatGPT (thinking mode) for a thorough prompt tailored to Lovable, stating you are selling to garage door owners and want a mobile-friendly web app
Paste it into Lovable and follow the suggested follow-up prompts
Use ChatGPT to generate the voice agent knowledge base/script (background, instructions, rules, script)
Click 'fix' when Lovable's readiness checks fail

quote.text: the best way to prompt a vibe coding app like lovable is to first ask ChatGBT to give you the best prompt for it for that specific tool.

tactics.name: Choose a high-ticket, after-hours niche without private-equity competition
steps: List high-ticket home services that get after-hours calls
Skip plumbing, HVAC and electrical because private equity has them
Pick a niche like garage doors, where fixes cost $400-$2,500
Target local suburbs so you can sell as a local

tactics.name: Urgency-based call forwarding workflow
steps: Give the client a dedicated or ported phone number
Create a GoHighLevel workflow that forwards the call only if the caller indicates urgency
Set secondary and tertiary numbers if the owner doesn't answer

lessons.lesson: A risk-free launch offer (no upfront, no contract, pay per closed lead) removes price as the reason a test fails; raise prices later.
Pick niches with high ticket sizes and urgent, after-hours demand that big players have not yet consolidated.
Voice AI that took venture-funded startups to build can now be approximated in minutes with templated platforms, so the moat is distribution, not the tech.
Use AI to write prompts for other AI tools; it saves time and gives more complete scoped builds.
Locality helps close: use a local number, city name and your first name so buyers see you as local even when you never meet.
Keep first messages short and ask a simple yes/no question, then pitch only after they reply.
The revenue extrapolation (200 customers x $500) assumes a 1% close rate from one tiny sample; treat it as illustration, not forecast.
Software builds are commoditised; the scarce skill is finding and closing customers, so spend most effort on selling.

evidence_quality.rationale: Live demo with real first-hand numbers for scrape cost and reply rates, but the sample is 50 texts, no customer paid, and the headline $100k/month is hypothetical. Chris has no prior operating history in this niche, and the segment includes a sponsor read.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Lovable sponsors the channel and Chris offers a referral link and promo code (TYC creator26); he also uses GoHighLevel, which is often affiliate-promoted.
